notes: ACTIVE relation pack (upgraded from pilot). No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional — not absolute anatomy. No Travell verbatim text. Companion MD: clinical-reasoning/shoulder-lateral-referred-differential.md, evidence/relations-shoulder-lateral.md, evidence/referred-pain-shoulder-lateral.md.

relations.source_structure: cervical nerve root / cervical somatic structures (C5–C6 pathway)
relations.clinical_context: Lateral shoulder pain with neck symptoms, dermatomal/myotomal clues, or poor reproduction on local cuff tests.
supporting_evidence: Cervical radiculopathy clusters (Wainner) support cervical contribution when present
Cross-region screening is standard when local tests fail to reproduce familiar pain

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Spurling more specific than sensitive; negative Spurling does not exclude cervical contribution.

limitations: Cervical contribution and RCRSP often coexist
Do not label as 'cervical confirmed' from one test
recommended_examination: Cervical AROM + Spurling / distraction / ULTT as cluster
Ask if neck movement changes shoulder pain
Repeat local cuff cluster for familiar pain

references.citation: Wainner RS et al. Reliability and diagnostic accuracy of the clinical examination and patient self-report measures for cervical radiculopathy. Spine. 2003.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT. 2017.

relations.target_region: shoulder girdle / scapular / lateral shoulder perceived pain
relations.clinical_context: Shoulder-girdle pain that changes with cervical movement; local cuff tests poorly reproduce familiar pain.
supporting_evidence: Fluoroscopy-controlled zygapophyseal provocation can refer to the shoulder girdle
Does not identify the exact segment from pain location in clinic

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Provocation maps are not Sn/Sp of Spurling or palpation.

limitations: Clinic cannot reproduce fluoroscopic provocation
Maps overlap between segments
Must not be used as Travell-style muscle maps
recommended_examination: Cervical AROM and radiculopathy cluster
Ask whether neck movement changes shoulder pain
Do not diagnose a facet level from a pain drawing

references.citation: Dwyer A, Aprill C, Bogduk N. Cervical zygapophyseal joint pain patterns. I: A study in normal volunteers. Spine. 1990.
Aprill C, Dwyer A, Bogduk N. Cervical zygapophyseal joint pain patterns. II: A clinical evaluation. Spine. 1990.
Fukui S et al. Referred pain distribution of the cervical zygapophyseal joints and cervical dorsal rami. Pain. 1996.

relations.source_structure: rotator cuff / subacromial complex (clinical RCRSP construct)
relations.clinical_context: Isolated Neer or Hawkins negative (or non-familiar pain) while history still suggests load-related lateral shoulder pain.
supporting_evidence: Impingement tests have limited diagnostic accuracy in isolation
Prefer cluster + familiar pain rather than single-test exclusion

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent numeric Sn/Sp. Literature shows mixed/limited standalone accuracy (Hegedus; Lewis RCRSP).

limitations: Negative special test ≠ structure cleared
Technique, irritability, and familiar-pain criterion matter
recommended_examination: Painful arc + Jobe/Full Can with familiar pain
Strength screen (drop arm / ER weakness)
Cervical screen if local cluster weak

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Physical examination tests of the shoulder: a systematic review with meta-analysis of individual tests. Br J Sports Med.
Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain: Assessment, management and uncertainties. Man Ther / related RCRSP papers.

relations.clinical_context: Jobe/Full Can does not reproduce familiar pain or weakness, but overhead load history remains suggestive.
supporting_evidence: Isolated empty-can / full-can performance is mixed; familiar pain and strength context matter
Cluster reasoning preferred over single-test exclusion

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp. Negative Jobe ≠ RCRSP excluded.

limitations: Pain inhibition vs true weakness hard to separate
Does not grade tear size
recommended_examination: Painful arc + Neer/Hawkins as adjuncts only
ER strength / drop-arm screen
Cervical cluster if local reproduction weak

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Br J Sports Med — shoulder physical exam reviews (qualitative mixed accuracy).
Lewis J. RCRSP framing — load history + familiar pain over isolated special tests.

relations.target_region: lateral shoulder / elevation and ER function
relations.clinical_context: Age/trauma + frank weakness (ER or elevation), drop arm, lag signs — beyond pain-limited strength.
supporting_evidence: Clinical tear clusters emphasize weakness more than pain alone
Does not measure tear size or completeness from bedside tests

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Qualitative cluster; do not invent Sn/Sp for drop arm or lag signs.

limitations: Pain can mimic weakness
Imaging/surgical decisions are clinician-led
recommended_examination: Compare ER/elevation strength and control
Drop arm / lag screens if safe
Cervical neuro screen if dermatomal clues

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Shoulder exam systematic reviews — tear-related tests qualitative.
Lewis J. RCRSP vs clinically important tear — weakness framing.

relations.clinical_context: Pain more at the point of the shoulder or with cross-body load; may be labelled 'lateral' by the patient.
supporting_evidence: AC pain overlaps RCRSP clinically
Isolated special tests have limited standalone accuracy (qualitative)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for cross-body or AC palpation.

limitations: Overlaps RCRSP and trapezius pain
Palpation alone is not confirmatory
recommended_examination: Localized AC palpation with familiar pain
Cross-body / high arc as adjuncts
Cervical and cuff cluster

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Physical examination tests of the shoulder — qualitative mixed/limited isolated tests.
Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain — overlapping anterior/superior constructs.

relations.source_structure: long head of biceps tendon (clinical construct)
relations.clinical_context: Pain more anterior; flexion/supination load may reproduce familiar pain; often coexists with RCRSP.
supporting_evidence: Speed/Yergason-type tests have limited standalone accuracy
Anterior pain is multi-source

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp; do not diagnose SLAP from one biceps test.

limitations: Overlaps RCRSP and labral constructs
Palpation of bicipital groove nonspecific
recommended_examination: Map familiar pain location precisely
Cuff + cervical clusters
Treat LHB as co-contributor hypothesis, not isolated label

references.citation: Hegedus EJ et al. Shoulder physical examination reviews — biceps tests qualitative limitations.
Physioguide shoulder-anterior / SLAP screen modules — no single-test SLAP confirmation.

relations.target_region: global shoulder pain / stiffness (may be reported as lateral)
relations.clinical_context: Progressive stiffness with limited AROM and PROM (especially ER); pain may be diffuse or lateral-sounding.
supporting_evidence: Clinical diagnosis emphasizes equal AROM/PROM limitation pattern
Differs from pain-limited elevation with near-normal PROM

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Clinical construct; imaging not required for early orientation. No invented Sn/Sp.

limitations: Early capsulitis may look like RCRSP
Diabetes / thyroid history relevant but not diagnostic
recommended_examination: Compare AROM vs PROM, especially ER in neutral/abduction as tolerated
Do not force aggressive stretch in high irritability
Cervical screen if neuro clues

references.citation: Kelley MJ et al. Shoulder Pain and Mobility Deficits: Adhesive Capsulitis (CPG themes). JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: History of dislocation/subluxation or apprehension in ABD+ER; pain may be labelled lateral by patient.
supporting_evidence: Apprehension–relocation clinical themes weigh history heavily
Special tests imperfect in isolation (Farber / Hegedus qualitative)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for apprehension cluster.

limitations: Apprehension may be pain-limited without true instability
Do not force end-range testing if irritable
recommended_examination: Mechanism + apprehension history first
Apprehension/relocation only if safe
Cuff strength screen

references.citation: Farber AJ et al. Clinical assessment of three common tests for traumatic anterior shoulder instability. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2006.
Hegedus EJ et al. Shoulder exam reviews — instability tests qualitative.

relations.clinical_context: When cuff special tests are inconclusive and palpation reproduces familiar pain in infraspinatus region — treat as hypothesis only.
supporting_evidence: Classical myofascial referral maps describe lateral shoulder patterns from scapular muscles (traditional class)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Palpation reliability for MTrP is limited; MTrP found ≠ proven cause.

limitations: Traditional maps are not absolute anatomy
High methodological controversy in MTrP diagnosis
Must not replace cervical/RCRSP reasoning
recommended_examination: Reproduce familiar pain with palpation + movement tests
Compare with cuff and cervical clusters
Reassess if no change after local treatment

references.citation: Tough EA et al. Variability of criteria used to diagnose myofascial trigger point pain syndrome — limited reliability/validity concerns.
Lucas N et al. Reliability of physical examination for diagnosis of myofascial trigger points. Clin J Pain. 2009.

relations.clinical_context: Load-related lateral shoulder pain plus neck contribution; dual familiar-pain reproduction possible.
supporting_evidence: Clinical coexistence is common; treating one region alone may fail
Negative Spurling does not rule out dual contribution

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence is clinical reasoning, not a single accuracy metric.

limitations: Do not force a single-label diagnosis
Prioritize red flags and neurological deficit first
recommended_examination: Document which tests reproduce familiar pain in which region
Treat/reevaluate the dominant reproducible driver first
Hypothesis-exploration if no change

references.citation: Lewis J. Rotator cuff related shoulder pain — cervical screen framing.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: History of overhead/elevation load + painful arc and/or provocation with familiar pain; strength preserved or pain-limited.
supporting_evidence: RCRSP is a clinical construct guided by load and familiar pain
Clusters preferred over any single special test

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: No invented cluster Sn/Sp; qualitative compatibility only.

limitations: Overlap with AC/cervical
Does not exclude important tear if frank weakness present
recommended_examination: Elevation load / painful arc
1–2 provocation tests ONLY with familiar-pain criterion
Strength screen

references.citation: Lewis J. RCRSP assessment framework.
Hegedus EJ et al. Shoulder exam reviews — prefer caution with isolated tests.

relations.source_structure: cardiac / visceral (ACS and related chest-pain pathways)
relations.clinical_context: Shoulder or arm pain with chest pressure, dyspnoea, diaphoresis, nausea, exertional pattern, or vascular risk — not a physiotherapy special test.
supporting_evidence: Chest-pain guidelines require urgent medical pathway when ACS features are present
MSK hypothesis must wait until safety is addressed

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety pathway, not a diagnostic accuracy claim for a physio test.

limitations: Not all referred shoulder pain is cardiac
Do not delay emergency care to complete an MSK cluster
recommended_examination: Stop elective MSK cascade if ACS/visceral features present
Urgent medical referral per local pathway
red_flags: Pain into arm/jaw with exertional or autonomic features

references.citation: Gulati M et al. 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain. Circulation/JACC. 2021.
